deep.reconstruction:
The page holds several separate threads. All belong to Gauss's work on elliptic integrals and functions, and on the arithmetic-geometric mean (AGM) and lemniscate (the next page is an AGM computation of M(sqrt2,1)=1.19814023473559220744).

(A) Fourier expansion of the complete elliptic integrand (top left).
Gauss sets f(q) = (1 - cos^2p cos^2q)^(-1/2) = 1/2 P + P' cos2q + P'' cos4q + ...
Differentiating in q gives cos^2p cos q sin q (1 - cos^2p cos^2q)^(-3/2) = 2P' sin2q + 4P'' sin4q + ... The image shows only 'cos q sin q'; the factor cos^2p must be supplied.
He rewrites 1 - cos^2p cos^2q = A - B cos2q, with A = 1 - 1/2 cos^2p and B = 1/2 cos^2p.
My fill-in: from (A - B cos2q)(-f') = B sin2q f, comparing coefficients of sin2nq gives
1/4 cos^2p (P^(n-1) - P^(n+1)) = 2n(1 - 1/2 cos^2p) P^n - 1/4(2n-2) cos^2p P^(n-1) - 1/4(2n+2) cos^2p P^(n+1).
This simplifies to 2n(1 - 1/2 cos^2p) P^n = 1/4 cos^2p [(2n-1) P^(n-1) + (2n+1) P^(n+1)].
This is the three-term recurrence of Laplace-coefficient type (s = 1/2). Gauss's right side matches this exactly. His left side reads -1/4 P^(n-1) + 1/4 P^(n+1): the sign is reversed and cos^2p is missing.
Purpose: since the mean of cos2nq over [0, pi/2] vanishes, int_0^(pi/2) dq/sqrt(1 - k^2 cos^2q) = (pi/4) P with k = cos p. The coefficients P^n thus give the complete integral K(cos p) and its companions, linking to the AGM computations of the adjacent pages.

(B) Spherical trigonometry (centre).
He starts from the law of cosines, cos a = cos b cos c + sin b sin c cos A. The struck line 'xy + sqrt(1-xx) sqrt(1-yy)' is cos(b-c) in algebraic form.
Let M be the foot of the altitude p from A onto BC. Then tan BM = tan c cos B and tan CM = tan b cos C.
Hence tan a = tan(BM + CM) = (tan c cos B + tan b cos C)/(1 - tan b tan c cos B cos C).
Multiplying through by cos b cos c gives (sin c cos b cos B + sin b cos c cos C)/(cos b cos c - sin b sin c cos B cos C).
Using cos c = cos p cos BM, cos b = cos p cos CM and sin BM = tan p/tan B, sin CM = tan p/tan C:
- cos a = cos b cos c/cos^2p - tan^2p/(tan B tan C);
- sin a = cos c sin p/(cos^2p tan C) + cos b sin p/(cos^2p tan B).
Both are correct.

Then the key construction: sin AB/sin AC = mu, p = sin AC, q = cos BC.
With the right angle at B, mu = sin C is fixed and cos b = cos a cos c. This gives sqrt(1-p^2) = q sqrt(1 - mu^2 p^2), i.e. 1 = p^2 + q^2 - mu^2 p^2 q^2.
This is the algebraic relation between sn u and sn(K-u) = cd u. A right spherical triangle with a fixed angle thus models complementary arguments (the Lagrange-Legendre spherical-triangle picture of elliptic addition).

(C) Addition theorem for cn.
The first attempt, (xy - sqrt(1-xx) sqrt(1-yy) sqrt(1-mu^2xx) sqrt(1-mu^2yy))/(1 - mu^2(1-xx)(1-yy)), is inconsistent. It is corrected to
(xy - sqrt((1-xx)(1-yy)(1-mu^2(1-xx))(1-mu^2(1-yy))))/(1 - mu^2(1-xx)(1-yy)).
This is cn(u+v) for x = cn u, y = cn v, modulus mu: sn = sqrt(1-x^2) and dn = sqrt(1 - mu^2(1-x^2)).
The special case mu^2 = 1/2 (lemniscatic) turns the radicands into 1-xx, 1-yy, 1+xx, 1+yy. The denominator becomes 1 - 1/2 + 1/2 xx + 1/2 yy - 1/2 xxyy, which is proportional to 1 + xx + yy - xxyy.

(D) Right half: lemniscatic and general 'sl-type' addition theorems.
The Euler-Fagnano form is sl(a+b) = (x sqrt(1-y^4) + y sqrt(1-x^4))/(1 + xxyy).
With cl = sqrt((1-x^2)/(1+x^2)), he divides by (1+xx)(1+yy) and passes to the form (x cl b + y cl a)/(1 - xy cl a cl b). He checks the denominators (1 + xx + yy + x^4 + y^4 - x^4y^4, etc.).
He then generalizes to the integrand dx/sqrt((1-xx)(1+mu^2 xx)) (cf. '(1+mu mu xx)(1-xx)'). The involution x' = sqrt((1-xx)/(1+mu^2 xx)) maps this differential to its negative, i.e. x' = S(K-u).
The addition formula is S(u+v) = (x y'(1+mu^2yy) + y x'(1+mu^2xx))/(1 + mu^2 xxyy) = (x y' + y x')/(1 - mu^2 x x' y y').
He computes (1+mu^2xx)(1+mu^2yy)(1 - mu^4 xx x'x' yy y'y') = 1 + mu^2xx + mu^2yy + mu^4 xxyy(xx+yy-xxyy), with the line 1 - mu^4 xx(1-xx)/(1+mu^2xx) yy(1-yy)/(1+mu^2yy).
The normalisation s = kappa/sqrt(1+mu^2) and the s, s', c, c' expressions ((sc' + cs' + ss'(...))/(1 + ss's'...), and 1 + (1-ss)/(1+ss) * (1-s's')/(1+s's') = 2(1+ss s's')/((1+ss)(1+s's'))) are the same computation in rescaled variables.

(E) Fragments.
- sqrt((1+alpha xx)/(1-xx)), xx + mu^2yy = cc and 1 + xx/(mu c(1-xx)) point to the ellipse arc (second-kind integral).
- The substitutions y eps/mu = x, x = 1/(y mu) are transformations of the integral.
- Binomial-series numerics (1/4 - 1/2*1/4 + (1*3)/(2*4)*1/4 - ..., 1/4 - 1/16 + 17/512 - 45/2048, -5/64 + 15/128 - 85/1024) and the fractions bottom left (1/2 + 17/32 + ..., 1/2 + 1/8 + 17/256, ...) are series coefficients. Their exact target cannot be determined with certainty.
- The marginal words (Pythagoras, 'Grundstoff', Algorithm, Logarithm) are doodles.
errors: Recurrence for P^n: the left side should be +1/4 cos^2p P^(n-1) - 1/4 cos^2p P^(n+1); Gauss has -1/4 P^(n-1) + 1/4 P^(n+1) (opposite sign, factor cos^2p missing). His right side is correct. Taken literally it would give the wrong factors (2n-3), (2n+3).
The derivative line shows '+cos q sin q' without the factor cos^2p (could be a transcription or writing omission).
The first cn-addition attempt with sqrt(1-mu mu xx) sqrt(1-mu mu yy) is wrong for x = cn. Gauss replaces it by the correct sqrt(1 - mu^2(1-xx)) form.
In the lemniscatic denominator the last term must be -1/2 xxyy (not -1/2 yy) to give 1 + xx + yy - xxyy.
Bottom-left and right-margin numeric series: too fragmentary to verify. Some denominators (e.g. 296) look miscopied.

results.what: Fourier cosine expansion of (1 - k^2 cos^2 q)^(-1/2) with three-term recurrence for the coefficients; constant term gives K(k)
results.modern_name: Laplace coefficients b_{1/2}^{(n)} / Fourier expansion of complete elliptic integrand
results.usually_credited_to: Laplace, Lagrange (celestial mechanics, 1780s); Gauss used it in the AGM/Determinatio attractionis context (1818)

results.what: Spherical right-triangle relations via altitude; tan a, cos a, sin a in terms of altitude p and angles B, C
Right spherical triangle with fixed angle C (mu = sin C) gives p^2 + q^2 - mu^2 p^2 q^2 = 1, i.e. the complementary-argument relation of sn
results.modern_name: Spherical-trigonometric model of elliptic addition (sn u, cd u relation)

results.what: Addition theorem for cn with general modulus, and its lemniscatic specialization mu^2 = 1/2
Lemniscatic sine addition sl(a+b) = (sl a cl b + cl a sl b)/(1 - sl a cl a sl b cl b), equivalent to Fagnano-Euler form
Generalization to dx/sqrt((1-x^2)(1+mu^2 x^2)) with involution x' = sqrt((1-x^2)/(1+mu^2 x^2)) and addition formula (xy'+yx')/(1 - mu^2 xx'yy')
results.modern_name: Addition theorem for a Jacobi function (cn/sd-type with modulus mu^2/(1+mu^2)) in 'tangent' form

deep.surprise_reason: Everything here (Fourier/Laplace-coefficient recurrence, spherical trig, cn and lemniscatic addition theorems, their generalization to a one-parameter family) is standard. Gauss is well documented as having had these in his elliptic-function and AGM work, so this is a routine working page.
